newsitem.title: USA: U.S. retailers' profits rose in Q2.
newsitem.headline: U.S. retailers' profits rose in Q2.

text.p: After-tax profits of U.S. retailers rose to 1.7 cents per dollar of sales in the second quarter of 1996 from a revised 1.3 cents per sales dollar in the first quarter, the Commerce Department said Wednesday.
Previously, the department had reported first quarter retailers' profits at 1.2 cents per dollar of sales.
By comparison a year earlier in the second quarter of 1995, retailers earned profits after taxes of 1.7 cents per dollar of sales.
Retailers generated total after-tax profits in the second quarter of $3.87 billion, up from $2.84 billion in the first quarter and up from $3.62 billion a year earlier in the second quarter of 1995.
The Commerce Department based its findings on quarterly financial reports supplied by 546 corporations.
Retailers had total sales in the second quarter of $233.25 billion, up from $225.34 billion in the first quarter and also up from $218.44 billion in the second quarter of 1995, the department said.
The after-tax figures are for retailers with assets of $50 million or more and are not seasonally adjusted.
